tour.name: New Orleans Private Tour: the French Quarter, the Garden District, a Bayou Swamp Boat & Jazz
tour.subtitle: The Big Easy in one private day with a local guide and vehicle: Jackson Square and the French Quarter, beignets at the riverside, the mansions of the Garden District and its above-ground cemetery, a boat ride in a bayou swamp among alligators, and live jazz on Frenchmen Street.

A boat ride in a bayou swamp, with alligators and herons
tour.overview:
Founded by the French in 1718, ruled by Spain and bought by the United States in 1803, New Orleans is unlike any other American city: a blend of French, Spanish, African and Caribbean cultures that gave the world jazz, Creole and Cajun cooking and Mardi Gras. Around it, the bayous and swamps of Louisiana are home to alligators, herons and cypress trees draped in Spanish moss.

This private day shows both with a local guide and a vehicle: the historic quarters of the city, a swamp boat ride and an evening of live music.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in New Orleans
• Type: private tour with local guide, vehicle and driver; swamp boat
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• The French Quarter and Jackson Square.
• The French Market and the riverfront.
• The Garden District.
• A bayou swamp.
• Frenchmen Street.

WHY THIS WORKS
Your guide brings the city’s layered history to life, and the vehicle links the city and the swamp, about 45 minutes away.

WHO IT SUITS
Music lovers, food lovers, history lovers and families.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For plantations, ask us for a tour along the River Road with the Whitney Plantation, which tells the story of slavery.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
New Orleans is hot and humid from May to September. Frenchmen Street music starts in the evening; the tour ends with an optional evening extension.

days.name: The French Quarter, beignets, the Garden District, a bayou swamp and jazz
days.description:
What to expect: the history, food and music of New Orleans and the wildlife of the swamp.

Your guide meets you at about 9:00 for a walk through the French Quarter, whose buildings, despite the name, mostly date from the Spanish period after the fires of 1788 and 1794, with their cast-iron balconies and hidden courtyards. In Jackson Square you see St. Louis Cathedral, the oldest cathedral in continuous use in the United States, and the Cabildo, where the Louisiana Purchase was signed. You have beignets dusted with powdered sugar and café au lait by the Mississippi, and walk through the French Market.

Your driver takes you along St. Charles Avenue, past its streetcar line and oak trees, to the Garden District, where wealthy Americans built grand mansions in the 19th century. You visit Lafayette Cemetery No. 1 or another historic cemetery, with its above-ground tombs, built because of the high water table.

After lunch (not included) – perhaps gumbo, jambalaya or a po'boy – you drive to the bayous outside the city for a boat ride through a swamp of bald cypress and tupelo trees draped in Spanish moss, where your captain points out alligators, turtles, herons and egrets. You return to your hotel at about 17:00. In the evening, your guide can take you to Frenchmen Street for live jazz in its clubs.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
09:15 – French Quarter and Jackson Square.
10:45 – Beignets and the French Market.
11:30 – St. Charles Avenue and the Garden District.
12:30 – Historic cemetery.
13:15 – Lunch break.
14:30 – Swamp boat tour.
17:00 – Back at your hotel.
Evening – Optional jazz on Frenchmen Street.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Alligators are most active in the warm months; in winter they are less visible.
• A cooking class or a jazz brunch can be added.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, local guide, swamp boat, beignets and coffee, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, club cover charges, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: beignets.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Will we see alligators?
faq.answer: Very likely from April to October; less in winter, when they are less active.

faq.question: Is the swamp boat private?
faq.answer: It can be private or a small shared boat, depending on availability; we confirm when you book.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: No, but beignets and coffee are. Your guide suggests a Creole restaurant.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the swamp. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. The French Quarter is flat; the boat requires a step.

faq.question: Can we visit a plantation?
faq.answer: Yes. We recommend the Whitney Plantation, focused on the history of slavery.

faq.question: Is New Orleans safe?
faq.answer: With a local guide, yes. As in any city, stay in busy areas at night.

faq.question: Can we join Mardi Gras?
faq.answer: Yes, but book very early; the city is extremely busy.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light clothes, comfortable shoes, a hat, sun cream and insect repellent.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: October to May. Summer is hot and humid.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary in the United States: 15 to 20 percent is usual for guides and drivers if you were happy with the service, but it is always your choice.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
